papers.title: From FAIR to AWARE: Data Readiness for Agentic AI in the Earth Sciences
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence in the Earth sciences is beginning to act: prototype agents already search archives, run simulations and draft analyses. Scientific data were curated for researchers who bring expert judgement; an autonomous agent cannot be assumed to supply it. Data can satisfy the FAIR principles and still mislead a machine acting alone. We propose that Earth-science data become AWARE (Actionable, Well-described, Auditable, Recipe-equipped, Epistemically labelled), an agent-specific requirements layer that extends FAIR, within a three-part agenda: AWARE data, bounded tools, layered validation. The ingredients exist across community infrastructure. We outline a staged, measurable path to adoption, intended to reduce silent error.

papers.title: Temporal Extrapolation of Elastic Seismic Wave Propagation in Layered Media Using Neural Operators
papers.abstract: Temporal prediction of seismic velocity fields beyond the time interval represented in training remains challenging for neural operator models. This study develops a coupled neural operator framework for stress-conditioned temporal prediction in layered elastic media. A time-integrator-embedded Deep Operator Network (TI-DeepONet) advances the velocity field through an embedded fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) scheme, while a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) learns a residual correction to the predicted spatial field. The two components are trained jointly in a predictor-corrector configuration. Prediction is initialized with reference velocity fields at the first two time levels and proceeds autoregressively, with reference stress fields and prescribed excitation supplied throughout rollout, including beyond the training interval. Four cases consider horizontally polarized shear (SH) waves in four-layer soil columns with fixed total depths of 50 and 280 m, excited by third-order Gaussian-derivative (DOG3) wavelets with central frequencies between 0.5 and 6 Hz. Layer thicknesses and shear-wave velocities vary across profiles. Evaluations on test profiles extend beyond the training interval by up to twice its duration. The predictions reproduce principal velocity arrivals and depth-dependent response patterns, with accuracy varying across profiles. Across the four cases, mean peak-normalized root-mean-square errors (NRMSEs) range from 0.53% to 2.31% over the full evaluation windows and from 0.61% to 2.82% over the extrapolation intervals. Both metrics use each profile's peak absolute reference velocity over the full evaluation window as the normalizer. These results demonstrate temporal velocity prediction under reference-stress conditioning for the tested configurations; autonomous continuation of the coupled velocity-stress wavefield remains to be established.

papers.title: Evaluation of machine-learning and deep-learning SPEI drought forecasts against persistence across timescales and lead times in Bangladesh
papers.abstract: Bangladesh, home to nearly 178 million people, is highly vulnerable to recurring droughts that threaten food security and rural livelihoods. Machine-learning and deep-learning models are increasingly used to forecast drought indices such as the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI). Most studies report accuracy without a persistence reference, although accumulated indices are strongly autocorrelated, and seldom test drought detection, longer leads or variation between training runs. This study forecast SPEI at 3-, 6- and 12-month timescales one to three months ahead for the eight divisions of Bangladesh, using ERA5 reanalysis checked against 35 Bangladesh Meteorological Department stations. Five models, XGBoost, CNN, Bi-LSTM, CNN-BiLSTM and CEEMDAN-BiLSTM, were trained with five seeds each, scored on accuracy, skill against persistence and drought detection, and interpreted with Shapley values. At a one-month lead, the CNN-BiLSTM and Bi-LSTM beat persistence clearly at SPEI-3 and SPEI-6 (skill 0.408 and 0.350), while at SPEI-12 a Nash-Sutcliffe efficiency of 0.872 barely exceeded persistence (0.850). Skill and detection could disagree: at SPEI-3 and a three-month lead, XGBoost had the highest skill (0.439) yet detected none of the 119 drought months. Only at SPEI-6 did the forecasts beat persistence significantly and match its detection at all three leads, with fewer false alarms. At SPEI-12, gains were small or absent and varied between seeds. The forecasts kept 76-80% of their correlation against station-derived SPEI and relied mainly on precipitation and lagged SPEI. Forecasts should therefore be judged on skill against persistence and detection across several seeds, not on accuracy alone. In Bangladesh, SPEI-6 forecasts can support early warning up to three months ahead and SPEI-3 forecasts one month ahead, while SPEI-12 is better suited to monitoring.

papers.title: SR-Agent: An Advanced Intelligent Agent for Seismic Data Restoration
papers.abstract: Field seismic data often suffer from multiple degradations, including noise contamination, incomplete geometry, low-frequency loss, and reduced spatial resolution, requiring different restoration operations. Existing methods mainly address individual degradations, while sequential application of task-specific models often relies on human experience. Although all-in-one models integrate multiple restoration tasks, they face a trade-off between generalization and task-specific accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a SR-Agent (Seismic Restoration Agent) containing three sequential stages: classification, restoration, and evaluation. For the first two stages, we design an intelligent classifier based on ResNet to identify the degradation types presented in low-quality seismic data, and the classification results are used as task instructions to activate the corresponding restoration models in a pool, which contains dedicated networks for different restoration tasks. For the last stage, SR-Agent can dynamically schedule the activated models and explore an optimal restoration path, rather than relying on a predefined processing pipeline. Specifically, we first develop a no-reference restoration-performance evaluation measurement by combining four parameters: seismic trace coherence, energy distribution in F-K domain, spectral smoothness, and high-frequency energy ratio. Second, the evaluation measurement is applied to quantify the restoration performance of different candidate restoration paths. Finally, the path with the highest evaluation score is automatically selected and then applied to input seismic data. The results show that, when multiple degradation mechanisms coexist, SR-Agent can effectively plan an optimal restoration path, achieving accurate and intelligent restoration of degraded seismic data.
